newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to take action if dlr hits 127-128 yen - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to take action if dlr hits 127-128 yen - MOF.

text.p: Finance minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka was quoted on Saturday by a Japanese newspaper as saying that Japan will act in the currency markets when the dollar rises to 127 to 128 yen.
The yen is currently hovering just over 126.
The Mainichi Shimbun reported that Mitsuzuka made the remarks to a meeting of cabinet ministers on Friday.
"Our understanding is that the dollar at 127 or 128 yen is an excessive depreciation of the yen," Mitsuzuka was quoted as saying. "It is necessary to deal with such exchange rates."

At his news conference on Friday, Mitsuzuka said only that his ministry would take appropriate steps against excessive movements in the foreign exchange market, without specifying a dollar/yen level which would prompt it to act.
On Thursday, U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said he shared Japan's concern about the yen's recent fall, but also reiterated that a strong dollar is in the U.S.'s interests.

Traders said Rubin's statement suggested Washington supports Japan's independent attempt to check a further dollar rally, but is reluctant to use its own money and that Tokyo would have to fight alone to halt the yen's slide.
